Set negative intermediate and final results to zero. This will remove ringing around mattes when using a filter that has negative lobes.

impulse:	no filtering - each output pixel equals some input pixel
linear:	linear interpolation between pixels
cubic:	smooth interpolation between pixels
Keys:	cubic a=.50, approximates sinc (*)
Simon:	cubic a=.75, continuous 2nd derivative (*)
Rifman:	cubic a=1.0, lots of sharpening (*)
Mitchell:	mix of sharpening and smoothing (*+)
Parzen:	approximating B-spline (+)
notch:	hides moiré patterns (+)
Lanczos4:	good for scaling down (*)
Lanczos6:	good for scaling down with some sharpening (*)
sinc4:	good for scaling down with a lot of sharpening (*)
(*) has negative lobes, can produce values that are outside the range of the input pixels.
(+) not interpolatory, changes pixels even when no movement.
upside-down (swap top and bottom)
mirror image (swap left and right)
output format

pbb
Normally any pixels outside the output format are clipped off, as this matches what will be written to most image files. Turn this on to preserve them.

Choose which direction controls the scaling factor:
none	don't change the pixels
width	scale so it fills the output width
height	scale so it fills the output height
fit		smaller of @i;width@n; or @i;height@n;
fill	larger of @i;width@n; or @i;height@n;
distort	non-uniform scale to match both width && height
If you select the [2] button you can scale each direction differently. You should change @i;resize type@n; to "distort".
Rotate image 90 degrees

to format	Convert between formats. The "image area" of the input format is resized to fit in the image area of the output format, and differences in pixel aspect ratios are handled.

to box	Scale to fit inside or fill a box measured in pixels. this is useful for making postage-stamp images.

scale	Scale the image. The scale factor will be rounded slightly so that the output image is an integer number of pixels in the direction chosen by "resize type"
